source.notes: European call option priced by Monte Carlo, set up for a pricing-EFFICIENCY analysis in the sense of Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering, Ch. 1. One standard normal Z is drawn per realization; the terminal asset price is simulated EXACTLY from the lognormal law S_T = S0*exp((r - sigma^2/2)T + sigma*sqrt(T)*Z), so there is NO time-discretization bias. Two estimators of the discounted payoff are computed side by side from the SAME draw: a plain estimator (est_plain) and an antithetic-variates estimator (est_antithetic) that averages the payoff under Z and -Z. A live closed-form Black-Scholes price (bs_price, built from the erf builtin) is the exact reference. Run with results_spec.final_stats = true on est_plain / est_antithetic / bs_price: FinalStats.mean is the price estimate, FinalStats.std is the payoff sample standard deviation, and FinalStats.ci_half_width is the Monte Carlo error ( z * s / sqrt(N) ). Efficiency = 1 / (variance * work): compare the two estimators' std at equal cost, and watch ci_half_width shrink as 1/sqrt(N) when you raise n_realizations. All prices in USD; r, sigma, T, Z are dimensionless (T is the maturity in years as a pure number). See OPTIONS_PRICING_EFFICIENCY.md.

elements.name: Spot Price
elements.description: Current price of the underlying asset (S0), in USD.

elements.name: Strike
elements.description: Strike price K of the European call, in USD. Default is at-the-money (K = S0).

elements.name: Risk-Free Rate
elements.description: Continuously compounded annual risk-free rate. Dimensionless (per-year, applied as r*T).

elements.name: Volatility
elements.description: Annualized volatility sigma of the underlying (dimensionless).

elements.name: Maturity (years)
elements.description: Time to maturity in years, carried as a pure number so the exponent (r - sigma^2/2)*T stays dimensionless. Independent of the cosmetic 1-step simulation clock.

elements.name: Standard Normal Shock
elements.description: One standard normal draw per realization. Drives the exact lognormal terminal price. -Z is reused for the antithetic estimator.

elements.name: Variance sigma^2
elements.description: sigma * sigma, reused by the drift term and by Black-Scholes d1.

elements.name: sqrt(T)
elements.description: Square root of maturity.

elements.name: Diffusion Scale sigma*sqrt(T)
elements.description: sigma * sqrt(T): the standard deviation of log-return over [0, T]. Also the denominator of Black-Scholes d1/d2.

elements.name: Log Drift (r - sigma^2/2)*T
elements.description: Risk-neutral log drift over [0, T]: (r - sigma^2/2) * T.

elements.name: Discount Factor exp(-rT)
elements.description: exp(-r*T): pulls the maturity payoff back to time 0.

elements.name: Terminal Price S_T(+Z)
elements.description: Exact lognormal terminal price under the shock +Z: S0 * exp(drift + diffusion*Z). Exact simulation => no Euler discretization bias.

elements.name: Terminal Price S_T(-Z)
elements.description: Antithetic partner: same draw, opposite sign. S0 * exp(drift - diffusion*Z).

elements.name: Payoff max(S_T(+Z)-K,0)
elements.description: Undiscounted call payoff under +Z.

elements.name: Payoff max(S_T(-Z)-K,0)
elements.description: Undiscounted call payoff under -Z (antithetic partner).

elements.name: Plain MC Estimator
elements.description: Per-realization plain estimator of the option price: discount * payoff(+Z). Its across-realization mean (FinalStats.mean) is the plain Monte Carlo price; FinalStats.std / sqrt(N) is its standard error.

elements.name: Antithetic MC Estimator
elements.description: Per-realization antithetic estimator: discount * 0.5 * (payoff(+Z) + payoff(-Z)). Same expected value as est_plain but lower variance because the two legs are negatively correlated. Compare FinalStats.std against est_plain to read the efficiency gain.

elements.name: ln(S0/K)
elements.description: Log moneyness, used by Black-Scholes d1.

elements.name: Black-Scholes d1
elements.description: d1 = ( ln(S0/K) + (r + sigma^2/2) T ) / ( sigma sqrt(T) ).

elements.name: Black-Scholes d2
elements.description: d2 = d1 - sigma sqrt(T).

elements.name: N(d1)
elements.description: Standard normal CDF at d1, built exactly from erf: Phi(x) = 0.5*(1 + erf(x/sqrt(2))). 1/sqrt(2) = 0.7071067811865476.

elements.name: N(d2)
elements.description: Standard normal CDF at d2.

elements.name: Black-Scholes Price (exact)
elements.description: Closed-form European call price: S0*N(d1) - K*exp(-rT)*N(d2). Deterministic (same in every realization), so FinalStats.mean equals the exact price. Bias of a Monte Carlo estimator = its FinalStats.mean minus this value; because terminal prices are simulated exactly, that bias is zero up to Monte Carlo error.
